operations.name: Mara Youngdahl

expected.name: Mara Youngdahl
expected.description: Mara Youngdahl was one of the "Moody Park Three," members of People United to Fight Police Brutality charged with felony riot over the May 7, 1978 Moody Park rebellion in Houston. The uprising erupted from outrage over the killing of José Campos Torres — a young Mexican-American man beaten by Houston police and thrown into Buffalo Bayou to drown in 1977, whose killers received only one year's probation and a $1 fine. The three co-defendants — Travis Morales, Mara Youngdahl, and Thomas Hirschi — faced more than 140 years in prison combined. At their 1979 trial they openly defended the rebellion as a justified response to police terror, and were acquitted.

operations.source: Worker national supplement, late January 1979, Houston January 13 demonstration photo montage, PDF page 5: https://washingtonareaspark.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/1979-01-Worker-NatlSup-HoustonRebellion-LateJan1979-English.pdf . Bilingual caption identifies top-center trio left-to-right Tom Hirschi, Mara Youngdahl, Travis Morales. Exact rectangular crop isolates middle person; no AI alteration. See CREDITS-batch888.md. Contemporary May 1979 reporting conflicts with existing acquittal field; portrait addition does not endorse that outcome, which is flagged.
